subject: HorizonPay inference fit: latency & throughput deep-dive (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Rivera <ellie@horizonpay.com>, Chris Dalton <chris.dalton@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: HorizonPay inference fit: latency & throughput deep-dive (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great conversation, appreciate the clear framing. Below is a concise recap of the pain, goals, initial constraints, and proposed next steps so we can align before the technical deep-dive. Please reply if I missed anything.

1) Pain points (from HorizonPay)
- Payment confirmation latency at peak windows is causing UX timeouts and retry storms (late-night settlements and batch windows).
- Cost spikes when models are run synchronously for high-concurrency flows (fraud checks + merchant messaging).
- Need to keep cardholder data and inference logs out of general cloud storage (PCI scope).

2) Primary goals
- P95 end-to-end response for single-turn decision API <= 250 ms; P99 ideally <= 500 ms during peak.
- Sustained throughput target: 200 requests/sec for the decision endpoint (burst to 800 req/sec concurrent for peak settlement windows).
- Reduce per-call inference cost via batching, caching, and quantized model variants.

3) Model & workload constraints
- Model family: medium-sized open LLM (~7B) for structured decision & templated text generation; occasional fallback to a small 1.3B deterministic variant for ultra-low latency confirmations.
- Typical request length: 32-128 tokens; tail up to 512 tokens for dispute summaries.
- KV cache effectiveness expected to be high for repeat merchant flows (we should quantify prefix reuse).

4) Compliance / deployment notes
- Preference for a private deployment in us-east-1 with VPC peering / private endpoints to minimize PCI scope.
- Audit logs retention and key management (KMS/HSM) required.

5) Suggested topology options (initial)
- Option A (Dedicated private pool): Redwood Private in customer VPC + dedicated GPU pool for the 7B model, autoscaling for settlement bursts, private logging to customer S3 (KMS).
- Option B (Hybrid): Hosted control plane + Dedicated inference nodes in a private subnet; fast fallback to a quantized hosted variant for non-PII flows to absorb bursts.
- Continuous batching + prefix/KV cache on dedicated nodes to reduce token compute while holding 95th latency SLO.

6) Risks & questions we flagged
- Network egress and VPC NAT capacity during settlement bursts — need HorizonPay network ops capacity numbers.
- Failure modes for model fallback: need deterministic routing policy so payments flows never block.

7) Next steps (owners & dates)
- Technical deep-dive call (30–45m) to validate topology and SLOs, share initial perf numbers: proposed week of Dec 6 — Sean to send calendar invite.
- HorizonPay to share: peak throughput windows (15-minute granularity), sample request sizes, and PCI scoping doc — Ellie (HorizonPay) to provide by Dec 3.
- Redwood to share: draft SLA workbook (attached), topology sketch, and cost ballpark for Dedicated vs Hybrid by Dec 4 — Monica (Redwood) owner.

Attachments: horizonpay-mvp-sla.xlsx (SLA workbook, draft), horizonpay-network-topology.pdf (sketch).

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Ellie Rivera <ellie@horizonpay.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HorizonPay inference fit: latency & throughput deep-dive (post-call recap)

Thanks, Sean — this is a helpful summary and lines up with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- PCI: we need to be explicit that any logs containing cardholder data must never leave our VPC; audit events about inference calls can be exported as redacted metrics. We will send a short PCI scoping note by EOD Dec 3.
- Throughput: the steady 200 req/sec is accurate; our settlement peak is typically a 45-minute window once per day where we see sustained 600–900 req/sec and very short spikes up to ~1.2k req/sec (1–5 minute spikes).
- Fallback rules: when the primary 7B model is overloaded, we need an explicit routing policy that fails over to the 1.3B deterministic model with a guaranteed response under 150 ms for confirmations.

We can do the deep-dive week of Dec 6 — Dec 10. We prefer Dec 8 or Dec 9 in the morning (EST). If you can circulate a 30–45m invite with objective/scoped agenda, that would be ideal. Also please include any perf artifacts you have for a 7B/1.3B family on similar infra.

Cheers,
Ellie Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering — HorizonPay
ellie@horizonpay.com
